subject: Post-demo: Dedicated sizing — latency & throughput decision notes
messages:
From: Ava Riddle <ava.riddle@clearscope.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2027 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Thanks — clearscope demo & sizing inputs

Thanks again for the walkthrough today — the demo clarified a lot. A quick recap of what we need for the business case so you can size Dedicated appropriately: 

- Workload: streaming token scoring for real-time document suggestions (mixed short prompts and long context).
- Target SLOs: 95th pct latency <= 180ms for streaming token arrival (end-to-end from request arrival to first token emitted), 99th pct ideally < 350ms.
- Throughput: steady-state 5,000 tokens/sec across all routes, with burst to 9,000 tokens/sec for short windows (under 5 minutes).
- Concurrency: ~120 concurrent streams (each stream sends short incremental inputs ~1–3 tokens per 50ms on average).
- Cold-start: < 120ms tail for warmed model variants; warm paths more critical than cold in our use case.
- Data & security: we will need Private/VPC later, but initial pilot can run on Dedicated in Redwood-hosted.

I've attached our internal load trace and a small sample prompt set. Next steps from our side: review your sizing recommendation and a pilot plan for a canary run. Can we get an initial GPU recommendation and a quick estimate of reserved throughput (tokens/sec) and concurrency headroom? Also please include any risks we should flag for procurement.

Attachments: clearscope-loadtrace-0909.json (attached), business-requirements-summary.pdf (attached)

—Ava
Ava Riddle

ava.riddle@clearscope.ai
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2027 18:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Thanks — clearscope demo & sizing inputs

Ava — thanks for the clear summary and the traces, that helps a lot. Below is a concise assessment and recommendation based on the profile you shared.

SUMMARY RECOMMENDATION
- Pilot hardware: H100 (80GB) nodes for the pilot. Rationale: better streaming tail latency under high concurrency and superior kernel throughput for long-context KV-cache workloads.
- Production mix: 70% H100 + 30% A100s (cost-optimized pool) if you want to balance cost and tail performance.
- Reserved throughput: propose reserve for 6,000 tokens/sec for the initial dedicated pool (this gives ~20% headroom above your steady-state and covers typical bursts).
- Concurrency target: configure autoscale guardrails at 150 concurrent streams with soft throttling on new streams at 200.
- SLO gating: start with 95th <= 180ms and 99th <= 350ms; include automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant when 99th breaches for >5 minutes.

KEY TRADEOFFS
- H100: best tail latency and headroom for streaming; higher hourly cost but reduces risk of 99th pct spikes during bursts.
- A100: lower cost, good throughput for batching-heavy non-streaming paths; less ideal for the low-latency streaming you require.

PILOT PLAN (proposed)
1) 2-hour sustained run at 5k tps + three 10-minute bursts to 9k (we'll run twice across different times of day).
2) Collect token-level latency (first-token and per-token tail), pipeline breakdown (network, decode, kernel), and KV cache hit ratio.
3) Validate cold-start patterns using ephemeral worker restarts.
4) Produce final SLO proposal and cost-per-token estimates for a 12-month committed plan.

ATTACHMENTS / ARTIFACTS
- initial-sizing-estimate.xlsx (pricing and reserve calc)
- rc-demo-latency-throughput-summary.pdf (brief with charts)
- benchmarks-h100-vs-a100.csv (internal microbenchmarks)

NEXT STEPS
- If that looks sensible, can we schedule the pilot for next Tuesday morning (09/14) UTC? Ben will send a short runbook and we'll need a single engineering contact from Clearscope with sandbox credentials.

Quick technical notes to add to Sean's plan: 

- Batching / streaming mixing: For your workload (many small incremental token inputs), enable continuous batching with a 10ms batching-window and prefer prefix-KV caching. This reduces per-token decode time and smooths throughput.
- KV cache: Keep a hot set pinned per-node. For H100 pilots we recommend reserving ~24GB of GPU DRAM for KV cache for long-context sessions (your traces show frequent >8k context windows).
- Quantization: Consider q4_0 for production if you need more units; pilot on fp16 and a q4 baseline to compare quality.
- Monitoring: We'll emit token-level histograms, per-route latency SLOs, and an alert if 99th exceeds 350ms for >5 minutes. Also add an automatic fallback route to a smaller-model variant for user-facing routes.

Attachment: brief-runbook.txt (outlined steps, contact points)

Ben
